subject.title: fix(full-release-validation): bound GitHub releases dispatch with timeout

question: Should the cross-repository release-evidence dispatch use a 10-second connect deadline and 60-second total deadline, accepting that a timeout can be ambiguous after GitHub receives the POST?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound and retry-safe at the receiver, but the acceptable deadline and operator failure semantics are release-policy choices owned by the release workflow team.

options.title: Accept the 60-second bound
options.body: Land the proposed deadline because normal dispatches are fast and duplicate or ambiguous retries reconcile safely by release id.

options.title: Use a longer total deadline
options.body: Keep the connection bound but increase the total deadline to reduce ambiguous timeout warnings during transient GitHub slowness.

options.title: Leave the request unbounded
options.body: Reject the change and continue relying on the surrounding job timeout for this release step.

recommendation.title: Accept the 60-second bound
recommendation.body: Land the proposed deadline because normal dispatches are fast and duplicate or ambiguous retries reconcile safely by release id.
